## Motivation: Why Siamese Networks for WSSS?

### Problem
MCTformer CAMs do not reliably highlight disease spots

- Class Activation Maps respond to the **entire plant**, not disease-specific features
- Attention heads capture general object saliency, not fine-grained pathology

### Hypothesis (from paper)
A **Siamese network** comparing a query image with same-class **reference** images can learn to amplify distinctive (disease) features through contrast

\vspace{0.3cm}
\begin{center}
\textit{"What makes this diseased leaf different from a healthy one?"}
\end{center}

## Original Fusion: ADPL-CAM Token Fusion

### Per FPN level $i$:
$$T_i = \text{GlobalMaxPool}(\text{ref\_features}_i) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times 256}$$

### Fused features:
$$F_{\text{fused}} = F_{\text{query}} + \alpha \cdot \sum_i T_i$$

where $\alpha$ is a **learnable scalar** (initialized to 0.1)

\vspace{0.3cm}

## Original Fusion: ADPL-CAM Token Fusion

### Critical observation
`GlobalMaxPool` reduces each $H \times W$ reference feature map to a **single vector** $\to$ all query locations receive the **same** additive signal

\vspace{0.2cm}
\begin{center}
$\Rightarrow$ \textbf{Spatially inert fusion}: reference cannot guide \emph{where} disease is
\end{center}

### Key takeaways
- **Fix was transformative**: +23.8pp from bug fix alone
- **More references help classification** (N=3: +3.9pp) but hurt localization
- **Heavy augmentation is critical**: prevents memorization of reference--query pairs

\vspace{0.3cm}

**Pattern**: more references + weaker augmentation $\to$ worse overfitting

The model has capacity to memorize reference--query correlations that don't generalize

## Key Finding: Reference Does Not Improve Localization

\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[
    node distance=0.5cm,
    every node/.style={font=\small},
    block/.style={rectangle, draw, minimum height=0.6cm, font=\small},
    arrow/.style={-{Stealth[length=2mm]}, thick}
]
\node[block, fill=green!15, minimum width=3cm] (ref) {Reference features $H \times W \times 256$};
\node[block, fill=red!20, right=0.5cm of ref, minimum width=2cm] (gmp) {GlobalMaxPool};
\node[block, fill=red!10, right=0.5cm of gmp] (token) {Token $1 \times 256$};
\node[block, fill=blue!15, below=1cm of ref, minimum width=3cm] (query) {Query features $H \times W \times 256$};
\node[right=3.6cm of query, font=\small] (plus) {$+ \alpha \cdot$};
\node[block, fill=orange!15, right=0.3cm of plus] (broad) {broadcast $H \times W$};

\draw[arrow] (ref) -- (gmp);
\draw[arrow] (gmp) -- (token);
\draw[arrow, dashed, red!60] (token) -- ++(0,-1.1) -| (broad);
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

\vspace{0.3cm}

**Every query location receives the same reference signal**

- Cannot tell the model: "this patch looks like a disease spot in the reference"
- Only provides a global class-level bias
- Equivalent to adding a class embedding, not spatial guidance

## Proposed Solution: Spatial Cross-Attention

Replace `GlobalMaxPool` $\to$ broadcast with **Multi-Head Cross-Attention**:

\vspace{0.2cm}

\begin{enumerate}
\item Pool reference features to $14 \times 14$ grid $\to$ 196 KV tokens
\item Flatten query features to $H \times W$ Q tokens
\item Apply `LayerNorm` to Q and KV
\item 4-head cross-attention: each query location attends to all reference locations
\item Gated residual: $\text{output} = \text{query} + \gamma \cdot \text{attended}$ \quad ($\gamma$ init 0.1)
\end{enumerate}

## Training Results: Spatial Cross-Attention

\small
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lcccc}
\toprule
\textbf{Run} & \textbf{Data} & \textbf{Fusion} & \textbf{Epochs} & \textbf{Val mAP} \\
\midrule
\texttt{n1\_heavy} (baseline) & PlantSeg & token & 80 & 0.859 \\
\texttt{n3\_heavy} (baseline) & PlantSeg & token & 57 & 0.898 \\
\midrule
\texttt{spatial\_n1\_ps} & PlantSeg & spatial & 80 & 0.797 \\
\texttt{spatial\_n1\_ps\_pv} & PlantSeg + PV & spatial & 80 & \textbf{0.888} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\vspace{0.3cm}

### Observations
- PlantSeg-only spatial: **0.797** vs token baseline **0.859** $\to$ --6.2pp
- PlantSeg+PV spatial: **0.888** --- extra data compensates, approaches N=3 token
- Gate $\gamma$ learned to **0.333** (from init 0.1) $\to$ cross-attention is actively used
- PlantVillage data ($\sim$33K extra images) is critical for spatial model

## Localization: Spatial Model Challenges

### Problem: `feat_chmean` is broken for spatial backbone

Channel means of spatial model features are **all negative**, clustered tightly:

\small
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lcccc}
\toprule
& \textbf{Mean} & \textbf{Median} & \textbf{\% below 0.5} & \textbf{Disease IoU} \\
\midrule
Token model `feat\_chmean` & 0.19--0.49 & 0.10--0.50 & 63--92\% & \textbf{36.50\%} \\
Spatial model `feat\_chmean` & 0.62--0.85 & 0.72--0.93 & 8--30\% & 17.87\% \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\normalsize

After min-max normalization, spatial model seeds are **nearly uniform** ($\sim$0.8 everywhere)

Best threshold collapses to **0.00** --- every pixel is predicted as disease

\begin{tikzpicture}[

\node[block, fill=gray!10] (bb) {ResNet50 $\to$ FPN $\to$ MSE};
\node[block, fill=gray!10, below=of bb] (merge) {Merge 4 FPN levels $\to$ $112^2 \times 256$};
\node[point, fill=blue!15, below=of merge] (A) {query\_merged \quad $112^2 \times 256$};
\node[block, fill=gray!10, below=of A] (xattn) {Cross-Attention with reference};
\node[point, fill=orange!20, below=of xattn] (B) {fused \quad $112^2 \times 256$};
\node[block, fill=gray!10, below=of B] (gap) {Global Avg Pool $\to$ $1 \times 256$};
\node[point, fill=red!15, below=of gap] (C) {Linear(256, 115) $\to$ logits};

\draw[arrow] (bb) -- (merge);
\draw[arrow] (merge) -- (A);
\draw[arrow] (A) -- (xattn);
\draw[arrow] (xattn) -- (B);

\node[lbl, color=blue!70] at ($(A.east)+(0.3,0)$) {Point A — unfused features};
\node[lbl, color=orange!70!black] at ($(B.east)+(0.3,0)$) {Point B — fused features};

\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

All seed modes take 256-ch features at **A** or **B** and reduce channels $\to$ one 2D heatmap

## How Seeds Are Computed from Features

Each mode **collapses 256 channels** at Point A or B into a single spatial map:

\vspace{0.2cm}
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{llll}
\toprule
\textbf{Seed} & \textbf{Point} & \textbf{Reduction} & \textbf{Intuition} \\
\midrule
\texttt{feat\_chmean} & A & $\text{mean}(C)$ & Average activation \\
\texttt{feat\_neg\_chmean} & A & $-\text{mean}(C)$ & Inverted polarity \\
\texttt{feat\_chvar} & A & $\text{var}(C)$ & Channel diversity \\
\texttt{feat\_l2norm} & A & $\|f\|_2$ & Feature magnitude \\
\texttt{cam\_classifier} & C & $W_{\text{cls}} \cdot f$ & Class-specific map \\
\midrule
\texttt{fused\_chvar} & B & $\text{var}(C)$ & After cross-attention \\
\texttt{fused\_l2norm} & B & $\|f\|_2$ & After cross-attention \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\vspace{0.3cm}

**Key insight**: A $\approx$ B for all reductions $\Rightarrow$ cross-attention adds no spatial signal

\normalsize

### Critical finding
**Fused $\approx$ unfused** features again --- cross-attention does NOT add spatial discrimination

### Why does spatial cross-attention NOT help localization?

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Classification $\neq$ localization}: the model optimizes multi-label classification loss, which only needs the \emph{presence} of disease, not its \emph{location}

\item \textbf{Channel patterns, not spatial patterns}: the backbone encodes class identity in channel activation patterns, not in spatially discriminative maps

\item \textbf{Gate is active ($\gamma = 0.33$) but for classification}: cross-attention helps the model aggregate class-level information from references, but doesn't need to be spatially specific to do so

\item \textbf{No localization supervision}: without any spatial loss (e.g., contrastive patch loss, segmentation pseudo-labels), there is no gradient signal pushing toward spatial correspondence
\end{enumerate}

## Summary of Findings

\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.48\textwidth}
\textbf{What worked:}
\begin{itemize}
\item Bug fix: +23.8pp mAP
\item Backbone features \textgreater{} CAMs (+18.7pp)
\item CRF refinement: +5.6pp disease IoU
\item Heavy augmentation for overfit control
\end{itemize}

\vspace{0.3cm}
\textbf{Best pipeline so far:}

SPDNet `feat\_chmean` + CRF(srgb=5)

\textbf{42.13\%} Disease IoU

(vs.\ 29.98\% MCTformer baseline without CRF)
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.48\textwidth}
\textbf{What did not work:}
\begin{itemize}
\item ADPL-CAM token fusion for localization
\item Multi-reference (N=3): worse CAMs despite better classification
\item Spatial prototype matching at inference
\item \textbf{Spatial cross-attention}: no localization improvement
\end{itemize}

\vspace{0.3cm}
??? Classification loss alone cannot teach spatial correspondence between query and reference
\end{column}
\end{columns}
